_comment: The detector-first decision rule's numbers (A36, amended A40; vision/rules.py RuleConfig).
The rule answers the three reporting classes only - C1_EMPTY, C2_ACTIVE_PLAY,
C3_MAINTENANCE_NON_SPORTING - plus UNCERTAIN, which is an abstention and not a class.
play_min and small_group_max are the facility's requirement, not fits. detector/imgsz/tiles
name the model the counts come from (vision/detector.DETECTORS): yolov8n at 1280, untiled,
chosen 2026-09-19 by experiments/detector_audit.py under the rule registered in A36.
require_ball_in_play (2026-09-21, reported from use) adds that the ball has to be in
play rather than lying on the grass: a ball that persisted across the burst but moved
less than its own width does not count. Measured in ball diameters, so there is no
threshold to fit - see vision/ball.py. Inert on a single frame, and the trace says so.
require_ball and require_motion make ACTIVE_PLAY something that must be SHOWN: more than
four people AND a ball seen in one of the burst frames AND people moving. A17 measured
cross-venue ball recall at 0.40 (0.06-0.89 by venue), so require_ball costs genuine
matches wherever the detector cannot see the ball - that cost is measured in
results/rule_frame_eval.csv, and these are switches because it is a decision.
require_motion is inert while motion_play_min is null, and the verdict's trace says so on
every frame rather than letting an unfitted requirement pass silently. Every threshold
here is fitted on venue_01 camera A only (WP9-T5) and then frozen: frozen_at,
frozen_commit and tuned_on record when, from what, and on which camera. While frozen_at
is null the worker refuses to deploy this file; experiments run against it, since
measuring an unfrozen rule is how it gets frozen.
